name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,673

clue.text: Leave rubbish out

blocks.note: out and off both mean away, not on

explanation.surface: An instruction to put the bin bags outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a household chore; to bunk off is British slang for skipping school or work.
explanation.definitionFit: To bunk off is to slip away from somewhere you should be, an informal way of departing early.

clue.text: Stake everything you raised, it'll get you nowhere

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: in poker a blind is a forced stake put in before the cards are seen

explanation.surface: A gambler is warned that betting the lot will not pay off.
explanation.walkthrough: The poker sense of 'blind' as a compulsory bet supplies the first word; 'raised' is a poker word too, but here it flips YE.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind alley is a dead-end street, figuratively any course of action that leads nowhere useful.

clue.text: November is a name for a month in Israel

blocks.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trivia fact: one Israeli month is called November.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a month name translation, but 'November' and 'name' each give just N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisan is the first month of the Hebrew religious calendar, falling in spring, when Passover is celebrated.

clue.text: Maybe bow as Roman ordered

indicators.note: putting things in order means rearranging them, so these letters are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: A Roman told to bow, as a subject would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' reads as bending at the waist, but it is the rower seated nearest the front of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: In a rowing crew the bow is the rower in the seat closest to the bow, so bow is one example of a rower.

clue.text: Inedible bit of fish discarded after I washed up

blocks.note: a fin is the part of a fish you don't eat
to shed is to cast off or discard

explanation.surface: Kitchen scene: fish scraps thrown away once the dishes were done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after I' places SHED after I; 'washed up' reads as dishwashing but means done for.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone washed up is finished, their career or usefulness at an end.

clue.text: Pizzicato presumably not mastered

blocks.note: pizzicato strings are plucked, so played without the bow

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a music teacher judging a pupil's plucking; the answer splits as UN-BOWED for the string sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbowed means undefeated and unsubdued, the spirit of someone never conquered or brought low.

clue.text: Employment around Neath 40% down, creating anxiety

indicators.note: a figure that is forty percent down has lost two fifths of itself
one thing placed around another encloses it

blocks.note: employment of something is its use
deletion: drop 40%, two of its five letters, from the end, keeping the first three

explanation.surface: Jobs in the Welsh town of Neath have fallen sharply, worrying locals.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath is a town in South Wales; five letters minus 40% leaves three, which sit inside USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is a feeling of worry or discomfort, a mild synonym for nervous apprehension.

clue.text: Modern industry having impact around old church

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it on both sides

blocks.note: a policy with bite has real impact

explanation.surface: New industry is changing an area around an old church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having impact' is a noun phrase in disguise: a rule with teeth has bite, real force or effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Biotech, short for biotechnology, is a recent industrial field applying biology to make products.

clue.text: Obvious wart girl treated with a bit of Euthymol

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so these letters are reworked
a bit is a small piece, here the opening letter of a word

blocks.note: Euthymol is a toothpaste brand; its opening letter

explanation.surface: A girl's prominent wart gets dabbed with a dot of toothpaste as a home remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Euthymol is an old British toothpaste brand; only its first letter joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Writ large means shown on a grand, unmistakable scale, so plainly apparent to anyone.

clue.text: Confusion reported in age

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so we want a word that is said the same way

blocks.note: a daze is a state of bewildered confusion

explanation.surface: Muddle-headedness is said to come with getting old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In age' looks like part of the surface about old people, but 'age' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Days can mean a period or era, as in 'in Victorian days', matching an age in history.

clue.text: Cover short curls in nice soapy bubbles

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its final letter
bubbling liquid churns and seethes, so the letters are thoroughly mixed

blocks.note: taken as written into the mix

explanation.surface: Hair in curlers covered with a lather of shampoo bubbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbles' looks like a noun for the foam, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance gives financial cover against loss, so a policy is a contract providing protection.

clue.text: Cloth cut from seam on the counter

indicators.note: counter means opposite in direction, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: coal mined is cut from the seam

explanation.surface: Fabric trimmed from a seam lying on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seam' and 'cut' suggest sewing, but the seam is a coal seam and 'cut from' it is what miners do.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy cotton twill fabric, the material of jeans, so a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Weird rites, secretive veils - like nuns?

indicators.note: something weird is strange and out of shape, so these letters are distorted
a veil covers what lies beneath, so one piece wraps another

explanation.surface: Strange ceremonies hidden behind veils, as in a convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veils' looks like nuns' headwear, but it is a verb: SLY covers the rearranged rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns are called sisters, so behaving like them is being sisterly, with a playful extra sense.

clue.text: Wash my kilt, spilling this?

indicators.note: spilt liquid scatters every which way, so these letters fall in a new order

explanation.surface: A Scot asks for the kilt to be washed after a drink was spilt on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a spilt Scotch is exactly what would make the kilt need washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt whisky is Scotland's national drink, just the thing a kilted drinker might knock over.

clue.text: Pleasant smell of one finishing on the toilet

explanation.surface: An air-freshener scene: a nice scent after someone has used the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the second piece after the first; lav is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant herb whose sweet scent is used in soaps, perfumes and air fresheners.

clue.text: Italians used to 16 check Scot's carrying 9 on vacation

indicators.note: a vacated place is emptied, so only its outer letters remain
to carry something is to hold it within

blocks.note: Ian is a typical Scottish name, so Scot's is IAN'S

explanation.surface: Italians accustomed to floods inspect a Scotsman's luggage on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is FLOODING, a reference to Venice's frequent high waters; the 9 here is just the number nine, not 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice in Italy suffers regular tidal flooding, so its citizens are Italians well used to it.

clue.text: Spring traps of that girl guide

indicators.note: a trap catches and holds something inside it

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring
her means belonging to that girl

explanation.surface: A season or a Girl Guide setting snares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl guide' reads as one thing, but 'girl' ends the pronoun piece and 'guide' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters on Everest expeditions.

clue.text: Fellow can row back to Wapping? Disaster

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: can is slang for toilet, as is loo
a row is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: Someone rowing a boat back to Wapping on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping is a riverside district of East London; 'can' and 'row' are nouns here, toilet and noise, not verbs about rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooding is a natural disaster in which water overflows onto normally dry land.

clue.text: Big blow recently from Brussels, note unfriendliness

blocks.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union

explanation.surface: A diplomatic setback from the EU, delivered coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big blow' reads as a setback, but it is a literal windstorm: Storm Eunice battered Britain in February 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Storms in Britain are given personal names, and Eunice was a severe gale that struck shortly before this puzzle.

clue.text: Green English youth taken in by trick

indicators.note: to be taken in is to be drawn inside something else

blocks.note: a con is a swindle or trick

explanation.surface: A naive young Englishman fooled by a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like it describes the gullible youth, but it is the definition, a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Celadon is a pale grey-green colour, named for the glaze on Chinese porcelain of that hue.

clue.text: Biggest purple people eater scoffed triplets for starters

indicators.note: starters come at the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: plum is a dark purple colour

explanation.surface: The Purple People Eater of the 1958 novelty song gobbles three babies as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purple People Eater' is a familiar phrase, but only 'purple' gives PLUM; the rest supply initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumpest means most rounded and well-fed, so in this sense the fattest, largest in girth.

clue.text: Wetland walk out of bounds for shepherd

indicators.note: bounds are edges, so stepping outside them strips the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A boggy path closed to the public, posted for a farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shepherd' is a verb here, not the farmer: to guide people in an orderly way.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal people is to gather and direct them into order, just as one shepherds a crowd.

clue.text: Squash cooked itself

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters come out changed in order

explanation.surface: A squash, the vegetable, cooked on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like the vegetable, but it is a verb meaning suppress.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash an objection is to stifle it, both meaning suppress or crush something down.

clue.text: Lady's shoe dry on way into field, not in the middle

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence into a field
TT is teetotal, abstaining from drink

explanation.surface: A woman's shoe stays dry crossing into a field, unless it stands in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in the middle' sounds like an instruction to drop letters, but it means the middle letter of 'not'; 'on' puts TT after the stile.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a woman's shoe with a very high, thin heel, named after the slender dagger.

clue.text: Gag, a very poor one snubbing women

indicators.note: to snub someone is to cut them, so a letter is cut out

blocks.note: a wretch is a miserable, unfortunate person
standard abbreviation for women, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A comedian's terrible joke that ignores female audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' reads as a joke, but it is the verb meaning heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to choke or heave as if about to vomit, which is exactly what retching is.

clue.text: Nearly all dissertations specified examples at hand

indicators.note: nearly all of something falls just short, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: An examiner notes most essays cited particular examples.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a mouthful for a simple pronoun pointing to things nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative pronoun points to particular nearby items, the ones being indicated close by.

clue.text: Area covering Thailand, miles away?

indicators.note: in a down clue covering means sitting on top, so this piece comes first
something sent away is gone, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: Siam is the old name for Thailand
standard abbreviation for miles, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A vast region including Thailand, a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a continent containing Thailand, far away from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the continent that includes Thailand, and to a British solver it lies thousands of miles off.

clue.text: Cool display from school head

definitions.note: a noun here: coolness of manner

blocks.note: a stand is a display, as at an exhibition
of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
a school is a shoal of fish
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours like Sheerness

explanation.surface: A headteacher's calm, unruffled presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' and 'head' suggest a headteacher, but they are a shoal of fish and a headland; 'cool' is a noun for an aloof manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Standoffishness is a distant, unfriendly reserve, the frosty manner meant by a cool attitude.

clue.text: Sailor meeting with spooks, barring a no-show

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so a letter is kept out

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a seance is a gathering to contact ghosts

explanation.surface: A sailor meets with spies, but one invitee fails to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooks' suggests spies, but here they are ghosts at a seance.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is a failure to turn up, so it is an absence from where you were expected.

clue.text: High bank of seats on right entering trireme?

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

blocks.note: a trireme is an ancient oared warship, a galley

explanation.surface: A trireme's tiers of rowing benches, with a man on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The rowers' benches of a trireme look like the definition, but the trireme is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery is the highest tier of seating in a theatre, a raised bank above the stalls.
